name: library-layer-references
body:
Reference direction across library layers: a `section` helper call and a `{{ template }}` layout-composition call are the references that name a template another layer contributes. A local template's `section` helper call resolves against the merged section namespace, so a local template invokes an external section template exactly as it invokes a local one (section-helper). A layout invokes another library layout with the standard `{{ template }}` action, naming the target by the layout name defined in example-layout-composition, resolved against the merged library's layout set — every slide and section layout, whichever layer contributes it — both at render time and at the load-time example check (example-layout-composition, template-language). A `{{ template }}` call executes the invoked layout in the invoking template's own namespace, and html/template fixes a namespace's function set when the namespace is parsed, so every layout in a namespace shares the one `media` helper bound for the executing template's layer: the invoked layout's `{{ media "<path>" }}` resolves in the invoking template's own owning layer, not the invoked layout's own layer. A `section` helper call is the composition that re-binds the namespace: it executes the target template's own layout from a namespace built with the target's own owning layer, so the section target's `media`/`theme:`-based references resolve in the target's own layer (section-helper). Every reference written directly inside a template or theme resolves within that template's or theme's own layer: the directly-executing layout's `media` helper, a `media:` URL, a `theme:<name>/` reference, and a theme's own CSS, layout and media files all resolve inside the layer that owns the executing template or theme, and each layer's media is served from that layer's own `media/` root. A `section` helper call's child arguments resolve against the merged section namespace like the call's target, and each child's own `media`/`theme:`-based references resolve in that child template's own owning layer (child-constructor). The external layer validates on its own as a standalone library before the merge: each external-layer template's layout executes in the external layer's namespace, so the external library's own references resolve within the external library alone (templates-dir-validation). A media-bearing external layout composed into a local layout with a `{{ template }}` call executes in the invoking local layer's namespace and resolves its `media` in the local layer; an external layout that reaches the local layer with media-bearing content is composed with the `section` helper, which binds `media` to the target's own owning layer. A reference from an external template or theme to a section, theme or media name that only the local layer carries is a templates error while the external library validates on its own and while the external template executes in its own layer (templates-dir-validation); an external layout a local layout composes with `{{ template }}` instead resolves its `media` in the invoking local layer. A reference from a local template or theme to an external theme or media name is a templates error, because a local template's `media` helper and a local theme's `media:`/`theme:<name>/` references always resolve in the local layer. A local template's `section` helper call naming an external section resolves, and the target's own references resolve in the target's own layer.

AC: a local slide template whose layout calls an external section template renders that external section; a local layout's `media` helper argument, a local theme's `media:` reference and a local theme's `theme:<name>/` reference each resolve to a file inside the local layer — its `media/` tree or one of its `themes/<name>/` directories — and a local theme's `theme:<name>/` reference names a theme in that same local layer; a local template or theme that references an external `media/` file, or a local theme whose `theme:<name>/` reference names an external theme, is a templates error; an external template or theme that references a section, theme or media file carried only by the local layer is a templates error naming the external template or theme while the external library validates on its own; a local template's `section` call passing an external-layer child resolves and the child's `media` resolves in the external layer; the external library validates as a standalone library with the local `templates/` directory absent; a layout invoking another library layout with the standard `{{ template }}` action, naming the target by the layout name defined in example-layout-composition, renders the invoked layout at render time and at the load-time example check, and both the invoking layout's and the invoked layout's `media` resolve in the invoking layout's own layer.
